events.title: Yersin discovered the Lang Biang Plateau
events.description: After a grueling expedition, Dr. Alexandre Yersin set foot on the Lang Biang Plateau. Recognizing the mild climate and beautiful landscape, he proposed to Governor-General Paul Doumer to build a resort station here, laying the foundation for the birth of Da Lat City.

events.title: Establishment of Dong Nai Thuong Province
events.description: The Governor-General of Indochina signed a Decree establishing Dong Nai Thuong (Haut Donnai) Province, with its capital located in Djiring (present-day Di Linh). This was the first province-level administrative unit covering the land of Lam Dong.

events.title: Establishment of the first Party Cell (Cau Queo Party Cell)
events.description: In the Cau Queo (Arbre Broyé) area, the province's first Communist Party Cell was established, consisting of railway workers and road construction laborers. This was the core leadership of the revolutionary movement of workers and laboring people in Da Lat.

events.title: Seizing power in Da Lat
events.description: The Uprising Committee of Lam Vien Province led the masses to seize the Governor's Palace, the Police Department, and the Treasury. The puppet government surrendered, and the Provisional Revolutionary People's Committee of Lam Vien Province was introduced to the public at the Ngoc Hiep Cinema.

events.title: Establishment of the Da Lat Joint Military Academy
events.description: The State of Vietnam government (pro-French) established the Da Lat Joint Military Academy (later the National Military Academy of the Republic of Vietnam). This was the largest active-duty officer training center of the Saigon army in the South.

events.title: Inauguration of the Da Lat Nuclear Reactor
events.description: The Da Lat Nuclear Research Institute officially operated the 250 kW Triga Mark II reactor. This was the first nuclear reactor in Southeast Asia, marking a step forward for atomic science in Vietnam.

events.title: The Tet Offensive in Da Lat
events.description: The Liberation Army launched a surprise, simultaneous attack on key targets such as the Military Academy, Tuyen Duc Sub-sector, and the Governor's Palace... Fierce fighting took place right in the heart of Da Lat City, causing heavy losses to the enemy and shocking public opinion.

events.title: Liberation of Bao Loc Town
events.description: After the Di Linh sub-sector fell, the enemy forces in Bao Loc panicked and fled. Our troops quickly entered and took over Bao Loc Town and the former Lam Dong provincial capital without major resistance, completely liberating the southern region of the province.

events.title: Liberation of Da Lat City
events.description: Faced with the thunderous attacks of our troops across the entire battlefield, the Saigon government and military in Da Lat - Tuyen Duc fled in chaos toward Phan Rang. The liberation flag flew over the Da Lat City Hall, marking the complete liberation of Lam Dong Province.

events.title: Merger of the new Lam Dong Province
events.description: Implementing the policy of the Provisional Revolutionary Government, Tuyen Duc Province (including Da Lat, Don Duong, Duc Trong, Lac Duong) and the former Lam Dong Province (Bao Loc, Di Linh) were merged into present-day Lam Dong Province, with its capital located in Da Lat.

events.title: Lang Biang Biosphere Reserve recognized by UNESCO
events.description: UNESCO officially recognized the Lang Biang World Biosphere Reserve. This is Vietnam's 9th biosphere reserve, affirming the exceptional biodiversity value of the Central Highlands' primary forests and the indigenous Gong culture.
